messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer acme-inc reports a sudden spike of 502/504s from Hosted API edge starting ~15:12 UTC. Happening only for long-lived streaming embed requests. Trace IDs: trace=acme-1832,trace=acme-1833. curl sample below. Attaching logs.

support-bot: Ticket #4567 created. Notifying infra-oncall.

infra-oncall: Looking. Do we have client request pattern? headers? any common tenant header?

alex: Customer sends repeated long streaming requests with X-Client-Session and chunked bodies. Sample curl:
```bash
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer skXXX" -H "X-Client-Session: abcd1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=embed-large
```

maria: I see 502s correlate with a sudden drop in upstream HTTP/2 window. Envoy logs show many "RST_STREAM 11" and "STREAM_CLOSED_WITHOUT_RESPONSE" around same time. Suspect inflight window / keepalive mismatch.

ben: Can you paste the raw envoy log snippet? Also sample upstream addr and trace id.

alex: envoy snippet:
```text
[2026-03-18T15:12:21Z] [trace=acme-1832] upstream reset: reason=STREAM_RESET code=PROTOCOL_ERROR flags=0x0
[2026-03-18T15:12:22Z] connection window decreased: initial_window=65535 -> observed=16384
[2026-03-18T15:12:23Z] host: 10.4.22.40:8080 overflow inflight=256 limit=240
```

sam: If upstream reduces SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE mid-flight we can see this. Recent kernel sidecar update rolled out? Any config change on midproxy that touches http2 settings?

infra-oncall: We rolled a patch to midproxy two hours ago touching keepalive interval. Rolling back to previous release to test. Can someone verify if customer requests are HTTP/2 (curl shows http2) and if ALPN mismatch happened?

alex: Customer confirms HTTP/2. Their SDK keeps connections open (~30+ minutes) and spikes connection count per tenant. We think keepalive/heartbeat mismatch + inflight window shrink caused envoys to forcibly reset streams producing 502/504.

maria: Short mitigation: enable streaming-fallback-route which forces shorter-lived upstreams (can add via routing override) — this reduces concurrency pressure. I can patch a canary for affected frontdoors.

ben: Also adding a temporary per-tenant conn cap and lower SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW on ingress to make window behavior conservative.

infra-oncall: Rolling canary now to 10% for eu-west frontdoors and enabling tenant conn cap for acme-inc. Will monitor.

alex: Customer accepted temporary workaround. Will follow up with ask: can we provide recommended client SDK settings (keepalive: 60s, max_stream_duration: 10m) and share a repro payload? I'll attach.

support-bot: Note updated ticket with mitigation steps and rollback link: https://deploys.redwood.ai/rollbacks?id=1234 :thumbsup: 

sam: Logging note: collect tcpdump of edge->midproxy and http2 SETTINGS frames if rollback doesn't clear. Ping me if we still see RST_STREAM.

alex: Thanks all — I'll keep thread updated. Closing loop once canary metrics stable (5m window).
